question: Should `channelData.openclawProgressKind: "tool-progress"` become a documented public Plugin SDK contract for cross-plugin progress suppression?
rationale: The bundled Codex and Slack plugins need a shared typed seam, but exporting it commits OpenClaw to an externally consumable delivery-affecting API whose permanence and semantics cannot be settled by tests or CI alone.

options.title: Accept and document the contract
options.body: Keep the generic public exports, document allowed producers and channel behavior, add contract tests, and require exact-head live Slack proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the signal private
options.body: Remove the public exports and replace them with a maintainer-approved internal shared seam if external plugins should not be able to trigger delivery suppression.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the PR open without landing until maintainers choose the long-term progress-intent ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept and document the contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic public exports, document allowed producers and channel behavior, add contract tests, and require exact-head live Slack proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans the Codex, Slack delivery, and Plugin SDK boundaries needed to decide whether this should become a durable public contract.
